messages:
Priya: Heads-up — seeing a cluster of tiny-gang pods stuck Pending in us-west2. Nodes report idle GPU but scheduler isn't placing. Pods all request local NVLINK=true in annotations. Anyone seen NVLink anchoring causing packing stalls?
Raj: Can you paste `kubectl describe` for one of the pods and the node labels?
Priya: sure — snippet: 
```
Events:
  Warning FailedScheduling  10s (x5 over 2m)  default-scheduler  0/24 nodes are available: 12 node(s) had taint {gpu.nvlink: required}, 7 node(s) didn't match Pod's nodeSelector, 5 node(s) insufficient memory.
```
Priya: nodes have `gpu.nvlink=true` label on a subset of rack-local hosts, but free GPUs exist on other racks. scheduler seems to prefer NVLink locality over packing.
Mike: That matches what I saw last week — we added a soft-weight for NVLINK affinity in the placement plugin to avoid cross-rack memory copies for KV-cache heavy workloads. Looks like the weight is acting like a hard constraint in edge cases.
Anna: Also noticed autoscaler hasn't been adding warm nodes for that AZ because of an egress window policy — backfill blocked until egress quota freed. So two factors: topology weight + provisioning delay.
Sam: Quick triage idea: for tiny-gang pods (1-2 GPU) we could relax NVLINK preference and allow non-local placement, then rely on prefix KV-cache to warm. Cheaper and lower backlog but may hurt throughput for some models.
Raj: Is there an easy experimental knob? Where is the NVLINK tie-breaker implemented — runtime or scheduler plugin?
Mike: It's in the affinity scoring function in the scheduler extension. We made it a +100 score which, for small pools, effectively filters out non-local nodes if score threshold bumped to top-n scoring. We can change it to +20 for a canary.
Priya: Can we try a canary in us-west2-rack3 only? That's where the backlog is worst.
Sam: Yes — propose: change score +100 -> +20 for pods annotated `scheduling.alpha.redwood.io/tiny-gang=true` and monitor evictions and p99 latency. Rollout as a scheduler-configMap patch to the canary scheduler set.
Anna: Also open question: cost tradeoff. If we break NVLINK locality, some requests will increase GPU-to-GPU interconnect cost (we bill internal egress as part of Dedicated). Might increase per-token cost. Need to quantify.
Mike: I'll run a quick sim on last 24h placement traces to estimate % of tiny-gang that would have been placed off-NVLINK and the expected p50/p95 delta.
infra-bot: Alert: us-west2-rack3 backfill queue length = 42 for tiny-gang pods (>=10m). Auto-scaler paused due to egress-quota cooldown. See https://infra.redwood/internal/alerts/uw2-rack3-queue
Priya: Thanks. If the canary looks good we can promote the scoring change cluster-wide and add a scheduler flag to opt-in by workload.
Raj: If we do change scoring, add a temporary admission controller to annotate historical-heavy KV-cache deployments to preserve NVLINK where it's most valuable.
Sam: Workaround for immediate relief: add `tolerations` on tiny-gang pods for nodes without `gpu.nvlink` to allow scheduling to those nodes — but that's intrusive on app config. Prefer scheduler-side fix.
Anna: I'll open a quick cost-impact ticket and assign to Mike for the sim + dashboard changes. Priya, please add example failing pod to the ticket.
Priya: added logs and pod yaml to ticket #INF-918.
Mike: Running sim now — will post numbers in ~30m.
Priya: TL;DR plan: canary scheduler score drop in rack3, monitor p99 latency + eviction rates, autoscaler egress cooldown follow-up, then cluster rollout if safe.
Raj: one more: add an alert split for "NVLINK-preference backlog" so we don't confuse it with general GPU congestion.
infra-bot: Note: create-alert runbook reminder scheduled for 2h.
Sam: Great — thanks everyone.
Priya: I'll coordinate the canary window and post updates here. :thumbsup:
